docs.title: MagicArray – API Reference
docs.text: The MagicArray class provides a complete pedagogical implementation of array operations, enriched with benchmarking and visualization hooks. This page documents each method in detail, with usage examples and expected outputs.

docs.title: Class Signature
docs.text:
class MagicArray:
    def __init__(self, data=None):
        ...
  • Parameters
  • data (list, optional): Initial array contents. Can include integers, strings, objects, or nested structures.
  • Behavior
  • Initializes with dynamic capacity.
  • Supports expansion/shrinkage with overflow/underflow simulation.

docs.title: append(item)
docs.text:
Add an element to the end of the array.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.append(4)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 2, 3, 4]

docs.title: insert(index, item)
docs.text:
Insert an element at a specific position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([10, 20, 30])
arr.insert(1, 15)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[10, 15, 20, 30]

docs.title: delete(index)
docs.text:
Remove an element at a specific position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([5, 6, 7])
arr.delete(1)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[5, 7]

docs.title: get(index)
docs.text:
Retrieve element at position.

Example

arr = MagicArray(['a', 'b', 'c'])
print(arr.get(2))

Output

c

docs.title: set(index, item)
docs.text:
Update element at position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.set(0, 99)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[99, 2, 3]

docs.title: linear_search(item)
docs.text:
Return index if found, else -1.

Example

arr = MagicArray([4, 8, 12])
print(arr.linear_search(8))

Output

1

docs.title: binary_search(item)
docs.text:
Return index if found (requires sorted array).

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 3, 5, 7, 9])
print(arr.binary_search(7))

Output

3

docs.title: traverse()
docs.text:
Return list of all elements.

Example

arr = MagicArray([100, 200, 300])
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[100, 200, 300]

docs.title: Sorting Algorithms
docs.text: Each sorting method returns a sorted array and records benchmarking metrics.

docs.title: bubble_sort()
docs.text:
Example

arr = MagicArray([9, 2, 5])
arr.bubble_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[2, 5, 9]

docs.title: quick_sort()
docs.text:
Example

arr = MagicArray([10, 7, 8, 9, 1])
arr.quick_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 7, 8, 9, 10]

docs.title: benchmark(algorithm)
docs.text:
Run algorithm and return metrics.

Example

arr = MagicArray([3, 1, 2])
metrics = arr.benchmark('bubble_sort')
print(metrics)

Output

{'algorithm': 'bubble_sort', 'time': 0.0001, 'comparisons': 3, 'swaps': 2}

docs.title: visualize()
docs.text:
Generate chart (PNG) of current array state.

Example

arr = MagicArray([4, 2, 7])
arr.visualize()

Output - Creates demo_int.png showing array contents.

docs.title: export(filename)
docs.text:
Save array contents to JSON/CSV.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.export("array.json")

Output - File array.json created with contents [1, 2, 3].

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
• IndexError → Raised for invalid index access.
  • ValueError → Raised for invalid operations (e.g., searching non‑comparable types).

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Open your terminal and run:

git clone https://github.com/AI-Alchemy-Hub/alchemy-magicstructures.git
cd alchemy-magicstructures

docs.title: Step 2: Local Editable Install
docs.text:
Install in editable mode so changes are reflected immediately:

pip install -e .

This will also install required dependencies: - NumPy ≥ 1.20 - Matplotlib ≥ 3.0

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Check that the package is installed:

pip list | findstr alchemy-magicstructures

Or test import in Python:

from alchemy_magicstructures import MagicArray
print("MagicArray ready!")

docs.title: Step 4: Run Demo Scripts
docs.text:
Try the examples provided:

python examples/magicarray_demo.py

Expected outcome: - A sample MagicArray is created. - Sorting algorithms run on test data. - PNG charts (demo_int.png, demo_str.png, etc.) are generated in the project root.

docs.title: Step 5: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If dependencies are missing, reinstall: bash pip install numpy matplotlib
  • If using multiple Python versions, ensure you are running the correct interpreter (python3 vs python).
  • For Windows users, run commands in Git Bash or PowerShell.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MagicArray is the foundational class in the Alchemy‑MagicStructures library. It is designed to help learners understand dynamic arrays and sorting algorithms through: - Core operations: insert, delete, update, search. - Sorting algorithms: bubble, insertion, selection, merge, quick. - Visualisation: automatic charts using Matplotlib. - Benchmarking: measure average run‑time of algorithms.

This class is the Milestone 1 (M1) deliverable in the course syllabus, serving as the entry point for exploring advanced data structures with practical examples.

docs.title: Why MagicArray?
docs.text: Most learners struggle to connect theory with practice. MagicArray bridges that gap by: - Providing hands‑on coding exercises. - Offering visual feedback (PNG charts). - Allowing performance comparisons between algorithms. - Serving as a foundation for later structures (stacks, queues, trees).

docs.title: Learning Goals
docs.text: By the end of this module, learners will: 1. Understand how arrays work internally. 2. Implement and test multiple sorting algorithms. 3. Visualise data transformations. 4. Benchmark algorithms for efficiency. 5. Prepare for more complex structures in future milestones.

docs.title: MagicArray – Tutorials
docs.text: This tutorial walks through all the methods of the MagicArray class in a single consolidated flow. Follow each section step by step to practise construction, access, searching, sorting, benchmarking, and visualisation.

docs.title: Create and Append
docs.text:
from alchemy_magicstructures import MagicArray

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.append(4)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 2, 3, 4]

docs.title: Insert and Delete
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([10, 20, 30])
arr.insert(1, 15)
arr.delete(2)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[10, 15, 30]

docs.title: Get and Set
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray(['a', 'b', 'c'])
print(arr.get(1))   # → b
arr.set(1, 'z')
print(arr.traverse())

Output

b
['a', 'z', 'c']

docs.title: Linear Search
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([4, 8, 12])
print(arr.linear_search(8))

Output

1

docs.title: Binary Search
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 3, 5, 7, 9])
print(arr.binary_search(7))

Output

3

docs.title: Traverse
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([100, 200, 300])
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[100, 200, 300]

docs.title: Bubble Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([9, 2, 5])
arr.bubble_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[2, 5, 9]

docs.title: Selection Sort
docs.text:

arr.selection_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

arr.insertion_sort()

arr.merge_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

docs.title: Quick Sort
docs.text:

arr.quick_sort()

arr.visualise()

docs.title: IndexError
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 2])
try:
    arr.get(5)
except IndexError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

Output

Error: Invalid index access

docs.title: ValueError
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
try:
    arr.linear_search({'x': 1})
except ValueError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

Output

Error: Unsupported comparison type

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
This tutorial demonstrated: - Construction and access methods (append, insert, delete, get, set). - Searching (linear_search, binary_search) and traversal. - Sorting algorithms (bubble, selection, insertion, merge, quick). - Benchmarking performance. - Visualisation and export. - Exception handling.

With this single consolidated tutorial, learners can practise every method of the MagicArray class end‑to‑end.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Alchemy‑MagicStructures is a pedagogical library designed to reimagine how learners engage with Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA‑1). By embedding every structure in a unified Magic* class identity, the library transforms abstract concepts into flexible, complete, and visual learning experiences.

docs.title: Core Philosophy
docs.text:
• Magic Prefix Identity: All classes begin with “Magic” (e.g., MagicArray, MagicStack, MagicTree).
  • Universality of Data Types: Structures can hold integers, strings, sets, lists, objects, or nested data.
  • Completeness of Algorithms: Each class implements all theoretically valid operations.
  • Dynamic Capacity: Expand/shrink behavior with overflow/underflow simulation.
  • Benchmarking Principle: Global feature to expose and compare time/space complexity.
  • Visualization & Persistence: Hooks to display, save, and export structures for clarity and sharing.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Core Classes: MagicArray, MagicMatrix2D, MagicMatrix3D, MagicLinkedList, MagicStack, MagicQueue, MagicHashMap, MagicTree, MagicGraph. Extended Classes (future phases): MagicHeap, MagicTrie, MagicSet, MagicDeque, MagicTensor.

docs.title: Value Proposition
docs.text:
• Pedagogical clarity: Learners see structures as complete, flexible, and visual.
  • Practical relevance: Bridges textbook DSA with modern computing needs (AI, ML, visualization).
  • Community contribution: Open source, extensible, aligned with AI AlchemyHub’s ethos of knowledge sharing.

docs.title: Roadmap Snapshot
docs.text:
• Phase 1: Core classes with operations, constructors, expand/shrink, benchmarking.
  • Phase 2: Visualization hooks, persistence, export formats.
  • Phase 3: Advanced structures + gamification features.
  • Phase 4: Community extensions and ecosystem integration.

docs.title: Glossary – Alchemy MagicStructures
docs.text:
• Magic Prefix: Naming convention for all classes (MagicArray, MagicStack).
  • Expand/Shrink: Dynamic capacity adjustment of structures.
  • Overflow/Underflow: Error conditions when exceeding or reducing capacity.
  • Benchmarking: Complexity metadata and runtime comparisons.
  • Visualization Hook: Method to display and save/export structures.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: Alchemy‑MagicStructures is a pedagogical Python library designed to provide learners with a complete, flexible, and visual experience of Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA‑1). This document outlines the functional and non‑functional requirements guiding its design.

docs.title: 2.1 Class Identity
docs.text:
• Magic Prefix: All classes must begin with “Magic” (e.g., MagicArray, MagicStack, MagicTree).
  • Consistency: Naming convention applies globally across the library.

docs.title: 2.2 Universality of Data Types
docs.text:
• Type Agnostic: Each class must support storage of integers, strings, sets, lists, objects, nested structures, and other Python data types.
  • Flexibility: Initialization should allow specifying element type or leaving it open.

docs.title: 2.3 Completeness of Algorithms
docs.text:
• Full Coverage: Each class must implement all theoretically valid operations.
  • Example: MagicStack → push(), pop(), peek(), isEmpty(), isFull(), getSize().
  • Example: MagicTree → traversals, insert, delete, search, height, balance checks.
  • Algorithm Metadata: Each method must expose its theoretical complexity (Big‑O).

docs.title: 2.4 Constructors
docs.text:
• Overloaded Constructors: Each class must support multiple initialization paths:
  • Empty structure.
  • Pre‑filled with data.
  • With specified maximum size.
  • With external source (file, list, set).

docs.title: 2.5 Dynamic Capacity
docs.text:
• Expand/Shrink: Each class must support expansion and contraction of capacity.
  • Overflow/Underflow Simulation: Attempting to exceed or reduce below limits must raise appropriate exceptions.

docs.title: 2.6 Benchmarking
docs.text:
• Global Benchmarking Principle:
  • Each algorithm must expose time and space complexity metadata.
  • Runtime benchmarking must be available for given inputs.
  • Comparative logic must allow learners to choose algorithms based on complexity.

docs.title: 2.7 Visualization & Persistence
docs.text:
• Visualization Hooks: Each class must support display and save/export operations (e.g., displayAndSave("TreeIMG.png")).
  • Export Formats: PNG, JSON, CSV, DOT (graph description).
  • Persistence: Save and reload Magic objects for continuity of learning.

docs.title: 2.8 Extended Features
docs.text:
• Interoperability: Classes should support transformation into one another (e.g., MagicArray → MagicStack).
  • Gamification: Optional badge system for learners completing operations.
  • Error Pedagogy: Simulate common pitfalls (null references, collisions, underflow).

docs.title: 3.1 Usability
docs.text:
• Clear, consistent API design.
  • Inline documentation for each method.
  • Immediate error feedback with descriptive exceptions.

docs.title: 3.2 Performance
docs.text:
• Efficient implementation of algorithms.
  • Benchmarking must not significantly degrade performance.

docs.title: 3.3 Extensibility
docs.text:
• Modular design to allow addition of new Magic classes (e.g., MagicHeap, MagicTrie, MagicTensor).
  • Open source contribution guidelines.

docs.title: 3.4 Portability
docs.text:
• Compatible with Python 3.x.
  • Lightweight dependencies; leverage mature libraries (e.g., NetworkX, Matplotlib) for visualization.

docs.title: 3.5 Reliability
docs.text:
• Robust error handling.
  • Unit tests for all operations.
  • Deterministic behavior across runs.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Deliver the first working release of the Magic*** library with core classes, complete operations, dynamic capacity, benchmarking, and documentation/tutorials.

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text:
• M1 – MagicArray
  • Design, implement, test, and package MagicArray class.
  • Include expand/shrink capacity, overflow/underflow simulation.
  • Document all operations (insert, delete, slice, search, sort).

  • Provide tutorials with examples (arrays of integers, sets, objects).

  • M2 – MagicMatrix2D & MagicMatrix3D

  • Implement 2D and 3D matrix classes with determinant, transpose, multiplication, inversion.
  • Visualization hooks for matrix display.

  • Tutorials: school‑level 2D matrices, university‑level 3D manipulations.

  • M3 – MagicLinkedList

  • Implement singly and doubly linked lists.
  • Operations: insertions, deletions, traversals, reverse, search.

  • Tutorials: linked list of sets, linked list of objects.

  • M4 – MagicStack

  • Implement push, pop, peek, isEmpty, isFull, getSize.
  • Benchmarking of stack operations.

  • Tutorials: stack of strings, stack of files.

  • M5 – MagicQueue

  • Implement enqueue, dequeue, peekFront, peekRear, isEmpty, isFull.
  • Include circular queue variant.

  • Tutorials: queue of tasks, queue of objects.

  • M6 – MagicHashMap

  • Implement insert, delete, search, collision handling.
  • Benchmarking of hash functions.

  • Tutorials: hashmap of student records, hashmap of sets.

  • M7 – MagicTree

  • Implement binary tree with traversals (inorder, preorder, postorder, level order).
  • Include insert, delete, search, height, balance checks.
  • Visualization hook: displayAndSave("TreeIMG.png").

  • Tutorials: binary tree of lists, binary tree of animals.

  • M8 – MagicGraph

  • Implement graph with adjacency list/matrix.
  • Algorithms: BFS, DFS, shortest path, connectivity checks.
  • Visualization hook using NetworkX/Matplotlib.
  • Tutorials: graph of cities, graph of social networks.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document outlines the tutorial philosophy and structure for each Magic class. Tutorials are designed to provide learners with *hands‑on practice, conceptual clarity, and progressive mastery of data structures and algorithms.

docs.title: Tutorial Principles
docs.text:
• Completeness: Each tutorial must cover all operations and algorithms relevant to the class.
  • Universality: Tutorials must demonstrate diverse data types (integers, strings, sets, lists, objects).
  • Visualization: Tutorials must include visualization hooks where applicable.
  • Benchmarking: Tutorials must show complexity comparisons between algorithms.
  • Error Pedagogy: Tutorials must simulate overflow, underflow, collisions, and other pitfalls.
  • Gamification: Tutorials should include challenges and badges to motivate learners.

docs.title: Tutorial Structure
docs.text: Each tutorial will follow a consistent format: 1. Introduction: Brief overview of the data structure. 2. Setup: Instructions to initialize the Magic class. 3. Core Operations: Step‑by‑step examples of all valid operations. 4. Visualization: Demonstration of display and save/export features. 5. Benchmarking: Comparison of algorithm complexities with runtime examples. 6. Error Simulation: Examples of overflow, underflow, or collisions. 7. Challenges: Practice tasks with guided hints. 8. Reflection: Key takeaways and links to related Magic classes.

docs.title: MagicArray
docs.text:
• Arrays of integers, strings, sets, objects.
  • Sorting algorithms (Bubble, Shell, Quick) with complexity benchmarking.
  • Expand/shrink capacity demonstration.
  • Visualization of array slices.

docs.title: MagicMatrix2D & MagicMatrix3D
docs.text:
• Determinant, transpose, multiplication, inversion.
  • Visualization of 2D and 3D matrices.
  • Benchmarking matrix operations.
  • Tutorials: school‑level 2D examples, university‑level 3D manipulations.

docs.title: MagicLinkedList
docs.text:
• Singly and doubly linked lists.
  • Insertions, deletions, traversals, reverse, search.
  • Visualization of node connections.
  • Error simulation: null pointer references.

docs.title: MagicStack
docs.text:
• Push, pop, peek, isEmpty, isFull, getSize.
  • Benchmarking stack operations.
  • Tutorials: stack of strings, stack of files.
  • Error simulation: stack overflow/underflow.

docs.title: MagicQueue
docs.text:
• Enqueue, dequeue, peekFront, peekRear, isEmpty, isFull.
  • Circular queue variant.
  • Tutorials: queue of tasks, queue of objects.
  • Error simulation: queue overflow/underflow.

docs.title: MagicHashMap
docs.text:
• Insert, delete, search, collision handling.
  • Benchmarking hash functions.
  • Tutorials: hashmap of student records, hashmap of sets.
  • Error simulation: collision resolution.

docs.title: MagicTree
docs.text:
• Binary tree traversals (inorder, preorder, postorder, level order).
  • Insert, delete, search, height, balance checks.
  • Visualization hook: displayAndSave("TreeIMG.png").
  • Tutorials: binary tree of lists, binary tree of animals.

docs.title: MagicGraph
docs.text:
• Graph with adjacency list/matrix.
  • BFS, DFS, shortest path, connectivity checks.
  • Visualization with NetworkX/Matplotlib.
  • Tutorials: graph of cities, graph of social networks.

docs.title: 1. Identity
docs.text:
• Library Name (working): Alchemy‑MagicStructures
  • Domain: Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA‑1 focus)
  • Core Concept: Every class begins with the prefix Magic* to unify identity and convey creativity, wonder, and pedagogy.

docs.title: 2. Purpose
docs.text: To transform the way learners engage with data structures and algorithms. Instead of static notes or textbook examples, Alchemy‑MagicStructures provides a living library where each structure is a complete, flexible, and educational entity.

docs.title: 3. Philosophy
docs.text:
• Magic Prefix Identity: All classes (MagicArray, MagicStack, MagicTree, etc.) share a common naming convention.
  • Universality of Data Types: Each structure can hold integers, strings, sets, lists, objects, or nested structures.
  • Completeness of Algorithms: Every class implements all theoretically valid operations (e.g., push/pop for stacks, traversals for trees).
  • Overloaded Constructors: Multiple initialization paths (empty, with data, with max size, etc.).
  • Dynamic Capacity: Expand and shrink behavior with overflow/underflow simulation.
  • Benchmarking Principle: Global feature to expose time/space complexity, enabling comparisons and adaptive decisions.
  • Visualization & Persistence: Hooks to display, save, and export structures (e.g., displayAndSave("TreeIMG.png")).

docs.text:
• Pedagogical clarity: Learners see structures as flexible, complete, and visual.
  • Practical relevance: Bridges textbook DSA with modern computing needs (AI, ML, visualization).
  • Community contribution: Open source, extensible, and aligned with AI AlchemyHub’s ethos of knowledge sharing.

docs.title: 6. Roadmap (High‑Level)
docs.text:
• Phase 1: Core classes with full operations, constructors, expand/shrink, benchmarking.
  • Phase 2: Visualization hooks, persistence, export formats.
  • Phase 3: Advanced structures (Heap, Trie, Tensor) + gamification features.
  • Phase 4: Community extensions, integration with broader Python ecosystem.

docs.title: 📘 Introduction
docs.text:
MagicArray is the foundational class in the Alchemy‑MagicStructures library. It is designed as an educational tool to teach data structures with a focus on: - Dynamic array operations (insert, delete, update, search). - Sorting algorithms (bubble, insertion, selection, merge, quick). - Visualization of array contents using Matplotlib. - Benchmarking of algorithm performance.

This class is the Milestone 1 (M1) deliverable in the course syllabus, serving as the entry point for learners to explore advanced data structures with practical examples.

docs.title: 📚 Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using MagicArray, ensure you have: - Python 3.8 or higher. - Installed dependencies: - matplotlib >= 3.0 - numpy >= 1.20 - Basic knowledge of Python lists and comparison operators (__lt__).

docs.title: ⚙️ Installation Guide
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install the package in editable mode:

git clone https://github.com/your-repo/Alchemy-MagicStructures.git
cd Alchemy-MagicStructures
pip install -e .

Verify installation:

pip list | findstr alchemy-magicstructures

Run the demo script:

python examples/magicarray_demo.py

docs.title: Class: MagicArray
docs.text: MagicArray(elements: list, max_size: int = None)

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Syntax Description Exceptions Initialization arr = MagicArray([1,2,3], max_size=10) Creates a new array with optional max size. — Insert arr.insert(index, value) Inserts value at index. OverflowError Delete arr.delete(index) Removes element at index. UnderflowError, IndexError Update arr.update(index, value) Replaces element at index. IndexError Search arr.search(value) Returns index of value if found, else -1. — Sort arr.sort(algorithm="quick") Sorts using bubble, insertion, selection, merge, or quick. ValueError Expand Capacity arr.expand_capacity(new_size) Increases max size. ValueError Shrink Capacity arr.shrink_capacity(new_size) Decreases max size. ValueError Display & Save arr.display_and_save("array.png") Saves visualization as PNG. — Benchmark arr.benchmark("quick", trials=5) Returns average runtime for sort algorithm. ValueError

docs.title: Example 1: Integers
docs.text:
from alchemy_magicstructures.magicarray import MagicArray

arr = MagicArray([5, 3, 8, 1])
arr.sort("quick")
print(arr.elements)  # [1, 3, 5, 8]
arr.display_and_save("int_array.png")

docs.title: Example 2: Strings
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray(["pear", "apple", "banana"])
arr.sort("selection")
print(arr.elements)  # ['apple', 'banana', 'pear']

docs.title: Example 3: Custom Objects
docs.text:
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name, grade):
        self.name = name
        self.grade = grade
    def __lt__(self, other): return self.grade < other.grade
    def __repr__(self): return f"{self.name} ({self.grade})"

students = [Student("Alice", 90), Student("Bob", 85)]
arr = MagicArray(students)
arr.sort("bubble")
print(arr.elements)  # [Bob (85), Alice (90)]

docs.title: Example 4: Benchmarking
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([5, 3, 8, 1])
print(arr.benchmark("quick", trials=3))

docs.title: 📖 Notes
docs.text:
• Mixed types (e.g., ints + strings) may raise TypeError.
  • Visualization adapts automatically:
  • Numeric → bar chart.
  • Non‑numeric → labels.
  • Benchmarks provide approximate runtime, not precise profiling.
  • All visualizations are saved as PNG files in the current working directory.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: MagicArray is the foundational class in Alchemy‑MagicStructures. It demonstrates dynamic arrays with complete operations, visualization, and benchmarking.

docs.title: Constructors
docs.text:
• MagicArray() → empty array
  • MagicArray([elements]) → pre‑filled array
  • MagicArray(max_size=N) → array with capacity constraint
  • MagicArray(source="file.csv") → load from external source

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
• insert(index, value)
  • delete(index)
  • update(index, value)
  • search(value)
  • sort(algorithm="quick")
  • expand(), shrink()
  • displayAndSave(filename="array.png")
  • benchmark(algorithm)

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
• size → current number of elements
  • capacity → maximum allowed size
  • elements → internal storage list
